title: Is Teaching English in Vietnam Worth It? (2026)
description: What Saigon teachers really earn and save in 2026, the catches in hourly contracts, and how Vietnam compares with Thailand, Korea, China, Japan and Cambodia.
h1: Is teaching English in Vietnam worth it? The money, the trade-offs and how it compares
intro: Yes, for the right person. Ho Chi Minh City has steady demand, a low cost of living and a legal route for teachers with a degree and two years of relevant experience, and a full-time teacher who rents modestly can save a real share of their pay. It is a worse deal if you need a fixed salary, daytime hours or free housing: most centre work is paid by the hour on evenings and weekends, and Korea and China often include housing that Vietnamese employers rarely do.
keyPoints: In July–October 2026 job ads, Ho Chi Minh City centres offered most new teachers {{vnd:430000-560000}} an hour; at {{vnd:450000-550000}} an hour, a full-time load of 78–95 contact hours a month comes to roughly {{vnd:35000000-52000000}} gross.

Under the 2026 tax rules, a resident paying 9.5% social and health insurance takes home about {{vnd:38700000}} from {{vnd:45000000}} gross. A frugal single budget runs {{vnd:14000000-17000000}} a month, a comfortable one {{vnd:25000000-35000000}}.
The catches: pay is usually per hour actually taught, centre classes run on weekday evenings and weekends, and public-school hours largely stop from June to August.

Korea's EPIK includes free housing and many Chinese employers add housing and flight money, which Vietnamese centres generally don't, but Ho Chi Minh City scores 29.6 on Numbeo's 2026 cost-of-living index against 64.5 for Seoul.

Teaching legally needs a work permit. Under Decree 219/2025/ND-CP the 'expert' route teachers are filed under asks for a bachelor's degree plus at least 2 years' relevant experience. Under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, working without a permit costs the worker {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} and can lead to deportation.

sections.title: Who teaching in Vietnam suits, and who it doesn't

blocks.text: Vietnam rewards teachers who want a big-city job market, low day-to-day costs and a job they can make legal with a degree. It frustrates people who need a fixed salary, Monday-to-Friday daytime hours or the largest possible savings.
It suits you if

items: You hold a bachelor's degree and can document **at least 2 years of relevant work experience**: the 'expert' test of [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://congbaocdn.chinhphu.vn/CongBaoCP/VanBan/2025/8/45798/58141-1-20251073-1074219-2025-nd-cp.pdf), which has governed work permits since 7 August 2025 and replaced Decrees 152/2020 and 70/2023. The usual proof is a letter from a past employer abroad; experience in Vietnam counts only through earlier Vietnamese work permits.

You want choice. Ho Chi Minh City had 1,961 licensed language and IT centres in August 2025 ([Đại biểu Nhân dân](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-nang-cao-chat-luong-nhan-su-tai-cac-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tin-hoc-10388655.html)), plus public-school programmes, kindergartens and bilingual and international schools.
You are happy teaching children and teenagers, mostly on weekday evenings and at weekends.

You care more about low living costs than a large package. On [Numbeo's 2026 mid-year index](https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/rankings.jsp?title=2026-mid) Ho Chi Minh City scores 29.6, against 43.5 for Bangkok, 54.3 for Tokyo and 64.5 for Seoul.

You are a non-native speaker with strong English. Decree 219 sets no nationality or native-speaker condition, although many ads still ask for 'native' or 'native-level' English. VUS, for one, says it considers non-native speakers who send an intro video ([VUS](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979)).

blocks.text: It is a harder fit if

items: You have no bachelor's degree. The expert route requires one, and [a TEFL, TESOL or CELTA](/teach-in-vietnam/tefl-tesol-and-celta-for-vietnam) does not replace the degree, and on its own it does not replace the experience; it is the education-side requirement on top (Circular 21/2018 asks language-centre teachers for a 'suitable' certificate, and '120 hours' is an employer convention).

You have less than 2 years' experience. How Ho Chi Minh City applies the rule to newer teachers is not published, so ask the employer which proof they will file for you and get the answer in writing before you travel. Our guide to the [requirements to teach in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/requirements-to-teach-english-in-vietnam) goes through each document.
Your main goal is saving hard. Korea's public-school programme and many Chinese employers include housing; Vietnamese centres generally don't.
You need a fixed monthly income, paid summers or daytime hours from Monday to Friday.
Heat, dense motorbike traffic and air pollution would wear you down.

blocks.text: Most foreign teachers in Ho Chi Minh City are paid by the hour. In July–October 2026 job ads, centres offered {{vnd:390000-600000}} an hour, and most new-teacher offers were {{vnd:430000-560000}} ([Vietnam Teaching Jobs listings](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/city/teaching-english-in-ho-chi-minh)). VUS's recruitment FAQ (undated) says most new expat teachers start at {{vnd:450000}} an hour gross, and that full-time means 20–25 teaching hours a week ([VUS](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979)). 'Up to' figures, such as ILA's {{vnd:500000}} an hour for new teachers, are ceilings, not starting rates.

blocks.text: A full-time centre load is about 78–95 contact hours a month in [a 2024 Apollo listing](https://www.seriousteachers.com/job_details/278256/0/vietnamesl-teacher-teachers-needed-now-in-vietnam-vietnam), which at {{vnd:450000-550000}} an hour is where the {{vnd:35000000-52000000}} gross range comes from. Licensed teachers (PGCE, B.Ed or similar) can move up to [international schools](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam), which pay more and often add housing and flights.

Ads rarely say whether a rate is gross or net, whether an 'hour' is 60 minutes or a 35–45-minute period, or whether planning time is paid, so ask all three before you compare offers. Bonuses help at the margins: Apollo advertised a KPI-based {{vnd:13500000}} end-of-contract bonus and a signing and relocation bonus of up to {{vnd:15000000}}. Vietnamese law does not require a 13th-month or Tet bonus; it is owed only if your contract or the employer's published bonus policy promises one ([Labour Code, Art. 104](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html)).

Tax and insurance take less in 2026 than before. Under PIT Law 109/2025/QH15, residents pay 5/10/20/30/35% on monthly taxable income up to {{vnd:10000000}} / to {{vnd:30000000}} / to {{vnd:60000000}} / to {{vnd:100000000}} / above, after a personal deduction of {{vnd:15500000}} a month ([KPMG summary of the new law](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/vn/pdf/2026/01/new-pit-law-en.pdf)). On a labour contract of 12 months or more you also pay 9.5% social and health insurance, on salary capped at {{vnd:50600000}} a month since 1 July 2026. Worked through, {{vnd:45000000}} gross becomes about {{vnd:38700000}} take-home for a resident, against about {{vnd:36400000}} under the 2025 rules. You become a tax resident after 183 days in a calendar year or in the 12 months from arrival; non-residents pay a flat 20%, so ask how your employer will withhold in your first months. The [salary guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-salary-in-vietnam) has the full breakdown.

sections.title: How much you can realistically save

blocks.text: Rent decides most of it. eno.vn's [HCMC Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) (snapshot of 10 October 2026, asking prices from live listings) puts the city-wide median at {{vnd:3900000}} a month for a room and {{vnd:6800000}} for a one-bedroom flat.
Listings, job ads and this guide still use the old district names. Since July 2025 official addresses use new ward names instead: Thao Dien, for example, is now part of An Khanh ward.

Built from those rents and current prices, a frugal single teacher renting a room spends about {{vnd:14000000-17000000}} a month. A comfortable life in your own one-bedroom flat, with more meals out and some travel, costs about {{vnd:25000000-35000000}}.

Set against full-time take-home pay of about {{vnd:30500000-44300000}} a month, the frugal budget leaves roughly {{vnd:13500000-30300000}} a month and the comfortable one anything from nothing to about {{vnd:19300000}}; [the cost of living guide](/teach-in-vietnam/cost-of-living-in-ho-chi-minh-city-for-teachers#what-you-can-save) shows the arithmetic line by line.

Those are full months. Across a year, hourly teachers lose income over Tet and, in public-school work, from June to August, so many land nearer the lower end. The 8% pension part of your social insurance is not necessarily lost: foreigners can claim a one-time payment when their contract ends or their work permit expires without renewal.

You also need cash before the first salary, because centres commonly pay monthly for the previous month's hours: roughly {{vnd:21400000-24400000}} if you start in a room, and {{vnd:48000000-60000000}} for a one-bedroom with a two-month deposit.

sections.title: The downsides the job ads leave out

blocks.text: Hourly pay and seasonal gaps

Part-time employees on a labour contract have the same rights as full-time staff under the [Labour Code](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html), but many hourly arrangements pay only for hours actually taught, with nothing for cancelled classes, public holidays or Tet closures. Public schools teach for about 35 weeks, opening on 5 September and finishing before 31 May, so agency hours largely stop from June to August ([MOET school-year framework](https://baolaocai.vn/bo-giao-duc-va-dao-tao-cong-bo-khung-ke-hoach-thoi-gian-nam-hoc-post905643.html)).

blocks.title: The mistake that costs teachers most
blocks.text: Multiplying an 'up to' hourly rate by a full-time load and treating the result as a salary. Before you sign, get the guaranteed minimum hours or pay in writing, whether the rate is gross or net, and what you are paid in summer and over Tet. The [contracts guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teaching-contracts-in-vietnam) lists every clause to check.
Evenings and weekends

Centre students are mostly 6–16-year-olds, so classes run on weekday evenings and all day at weekends ([VUS](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979)). Weekday mornings are free, but evenings out and weekend trips are hard. Daytime Monday-to-Friday work exists in public-school placements, kindergartens and bilingual and international schools; see [workload and schedules](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-workload-and-schedules-in-vietnam).
Paperwork that takes weeks to months

Your employer files the work permit 60 to 10 days before your start date; the decree allows up to 10 working days for a decision, and Ho Chi Minh City publishes 5. You supply a degree, proof of experience, a criminal record issued no more than 6 months before filing and a health check, which in practice is done in Vietnam. Vietnam joined the Apostille Convention with effect from 11 September 2026 (Decree 293/2026/ND-CP): documents from member countries need an apostille, while documents from non-member countries, from Germany, Austria and Czechia, and from Thailand until 28 February 2027, still need consular legalisation ([HCCH status table](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41)). Changing employer means a new permit, even for the same job.

Your employer arranges the rest of your paperwork once your work permit is issued; ask them exactly what they cover and what it costs. The [work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers) walks through the whole file, and your employer and the authority have the final word.
Traffic, heat, floods and air

Saigon is a hot motorbike city where some streets flood in heavy rain and at high tides. On Numbeo's perception-based 2026 quality-of-life data, Ho Chi Minh City's pollution score is 92.1, against 47.6 for Seoul and 42.5 for Tokyo, and its commute-time score (32.1) is worse than Hanoi's (27.7) ([Numbeo](https://www.numbeo.com/quality-of-life/rankings.jsp?title=2026-mid)). Riding legally needs a licence that is valid in Vietnam, which many home licences are not.
Employers that fail

Centres that take tuition up front can collapse owing wages: a group of at least 81 foreign teachers said the Apax Leaders chain owed them {{vnd:13400000000}} in total ([Stockbiz](https://stockbiz.vn/tin-tuc/ibc-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai-het-hy-vong-duoc-apax-leaders-tra-no-luong/24554112)). The law is on your side: final pay is due within 14 working days of a contract ending, and an employer may not keep your original documents or take a deposit from you. Check the employer before you sign (step 4 below).

blocks.text: Headline salaries mislead across borders: exchange rates move, and the biggest difference is whether housing and flights come with the job. The table keeps each country's pay in its own currency, as employers publish it, and compares living costs with Numbeo's 2026 mid-year cost-of-living index (New York = 100, rent excluded).

blocks.text: Vietnam or Thailand

Bangkok costs noticeably more to live in than Ho Chi Minh City (43.5 against 29.6), and we could not verify a typical 2026 Thai salary, so compare real offers net of rent. Paperwork differs too: Thailand applies the Apostille Convention only from 28 February 2027 ([HCCH](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41)), so until then expect your degree and criminal record to need embassy authentication, while Vietnam has accepted apostilles since September 2026.
Vietnam or South Korea

Korea's public-school programme wins on structure: a salaried contract, free leased housing, a ₩300,000 settlement allowance, a ₩1.3M completion bonus in most provinces and about a month's salary as severance ([EPIK salary and benefits](https://www.epik.go.kr/web/epik/contents/Salarybenefits)). It loses on access: only citizens of seven countries qualify ([EPIK eligibility](https://www.epik.go.kr/web/epik/contents/Eligibility)), and Korea's demand for foreign English teachers is falling, with AI learning tools cited as one cause (Korea JoongAng Daily, 7 May 2026, from Ministry of Justice data).
Vietnam or China

Chinese employers commonly add housing and a yearly flight allowance ([example 2026 posting](https://beta.teast.co/job/myp-english-teacher-pudong-shanghai-sep-2026-start-Uh2LeDzN0i6xUEmWhv0D)), which changes the savings maths. The bar is higher: China's route expects a native speaker teaching their own language, a degree and 2 years' teaching experience unless a TEFL/TESOL, education degree or teaching licence waives it ([Australian Department of Education](https://www.education.gov.au/node/12100)). Vietnam's rules are qualification-based, with no passport list.
Vietnam or Japan

JET pays a fixed ¥4,020,000 in year one under rates applied from April 2025, with income tax, resident tax and social insurance deducted, and covers travel to and from Japan ([Embassy of Japan in India](https://www.in.emb-japan.go.jp/itpr_ja/11_000001_01196.html)). It recruits once a year, while Vietnamese centres hire all year. Tokyo's cost index (54.3) is almost double Ho Chi Minh City's.
Vietnam or Cambodia

Cambodia has the lowest bar, with no legal degree requirement, but private schools and centres pay about US$700–1,500 a month, and Phnom Penh is more expensive than Ho Chi Minh City on Numbeo's index (37.4 against 29.6). Work permits run by calendar year through the FWCMS portal, and a foreigner working without one risks up to 3 months' imprisonment or deportation, on top of fines for the employer ([DFDL](https://www.dfdl.com/insights/legal-and-tax-updates/cambodia-foreign-work-permit-application-deadline-is-approaching/)).
Within Vietnam, Hanoi is slightly cheaper on Numbeo's index (28.3), the Hanoi ads we checked from July–October 2026 paid the same as or slightly more than Saigon's, and Saigon has the most jobs.
Demand is solid but this is not a hiring boom for foreigners, and the city has started checking foreign teachers' papers.

items: **English from Grade 1 by 2030.** [Decision 2371/QĐ-TTg](https://en.baochinhphu.vn/english-to-become-compulsory-language-from-grade-1-nationwide-by-2030-111251031143422078.htm) (27 October 2025) makes English compulsory from Grade 1 nationwide by 2030; it now starts at Grade 3. MOET estimated it needs about 12,000 more preschool and nearly 10,000 more primary English teachers, which are Vietnamese public-sector posts; letting foreigners teach in public schools is only a policy to be studied.

**Ho Chi Minh City's pilot.** In June 2026 the city approved a 2026–2030 pilot letting 246 public preschools and schools recruit directly and contract foreign teachers ([Giáo dục Việt Nam](https://giaoduc.net.vn/tphcm-246-truong-mam-non-pho-thong-duoc-tu-tuyen-giao-vien-hop-dong-voi-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai-post260905.gd)). The approval gave no salary or budget figures, and it is not yet clear whether any school will contract foreign teachers directly in 2026–27, so treat it as a future opening rather than today's jobs.

**Paperwork checks.** In October 2025 the city education department told its centres to manage foreign teachers by the rules, and in January 2026 it ordered schools running linked English programmes to vet their foreign teachers' papers, including work permits and certified degrees ([Đại biểu Nhân dân](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-ra-soat-nang-luc-bang-cap-giao-vien-chuong-trinh-lien-ket-10402625.html)). Don't rely on old forum claims that 'nobody checks'.

**A new penalty decree.** Since 10 September 2026, Decree 283/2026/ND-CP fines a foreign worker without a valid permit {{vnd:15000000-25000000}}, and the worker may be deported ([report on the decree](https://suckhoedoisong.vn/tu-10-9-2026-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-se-bi-phat-neu-khong-co-giay-phep-lao-dong-169260824224738.htm)). An employer that files altered or forged documents is fined {{vnd:40000000-60000000}} ({{vnd:80000000-120000000}} for a company, school or centre), so never let anyone submit an experience letter that is not true.
**Simpler documents, more take-home pay.** The Apostille Convention has applied to Vietnam since 11 September 2026, and the 2026 tax changes raised the personal deduction to {{vnd:15500000}} a month.

**AI.** In Vietnam the evidence that AI is replacing teachers is anecdotal: one corporate programme switched to AI voice instruction, while educators describe AI as a complement, and most parents still prefer in-person classes ([Tuổi Trẻ News](https://news.tuoitre.vn/is-ai-replacing-english-teachers-in-vietnam-103250915151348453.htm)).

items.title: Confirm you can get a work permit
items.text: Check your degree and how you will prove 2 years' relevant experience. With less than that, ask the employer in writing which proof they will file before you book anything.

items.title: Turn the offer into a monthly net figure
items.text: Multiply the hourly rate by the hours you are guaranteed, not promised, then take off 9.5% insurance (on a 12-month contract) and income tax. Ask whether the rate is gross or net and per 60-minute hour.

items.title: Check where the job actually is
items.text: Since July 2025 Ho Chi Minh City includes former Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau, so an ad tagged 'HCMC' can be 30–200+ km from District 1. Ask for the campus address and its new ward name.

items.title: Check the employer
items.text: Ask to see its operating licence, see whether teachers have reviewed it in eno.vn's [school directory](/schools) (most schools have few or no reviews yet), and compare current postings on [eno.vn's jobs page](/jobs-vietnam-expats). Never pay to get a job.

items.title: Bring a cash buffer
items.text: Plan for one to two months of living costs plus a rental deposit, because the first salary usually arrives a month or more after you start.

faqs.q: Can you save money teaching English in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Yes, if you rent a room or share and teach a full load: on 2026 pay ads and budgets, a frugal full-time teacher in Ho Chi Minh City can keep roughly 45 to 70 percent of take-home pay in a full month. Living alone in a one-bedroom flat with a comfortable lifestyle can leave little, especially in months with fewer hours.

faqs.q: Is Vietnam or Thailand better for a first teaching job?
faqs.a: Vietnam is cheaper to live in on Numbeo's 2026 index, its work-permit rules are qualification-based with no nationality list, and it accepts apostilled documents from most Apostille Convention countries. Thailand applies the apostille only from 28 February 2027. Compare actual offers net of rent before deciding.

faqs.q: Is South Korea better than Vietnam for saving money?
faqs.a: Often, if you qualify: Korea's EPIK includes free leased housing, a settlement allowance and, in most provinces, a completion bonus, so rent does not eat into pay. Only citizens of seven English-speaking countries can apply, degree-only applicants are not being hired in 2026, and Korean demand for foreign teachers is falling.

faqs.q: Can I teach English in Vietnam without a degree?
faqs.a: Not on the standard legal route: the work permit's expert category requires a bachelor's degree plus two years of relevant experience, and working without a permit brings a fine and possible deportation under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP. Cambodia has no legal degree requirement but pays less.

faqs.q: Can non-native English speakers teach in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Yes, legally: Decree 219/2025/ND-CP sets no nationality or native-speaker condition. Many ads still ask for native or native-level English, so target employers that ask for a level rather than a passport, and keep an IELTS or other C1 result ready.

faqs.q: Will compulsory English from Grade 1 create lots of jobs for foreign teachers?
faqs.a: Not directly. The national plan relies on training and hiring Vietnamese teachers; foreign teachers in public schools are only a policy to be studied. Ho Chi Minh City's 246-school pilot could open direct public-school contracts, but it is not yet clear when schools will start hiring that way.
